What we did (simple words): Quantum computers will break today's encryption (RSA, ECC). Code must be moved to new quantum-safe encryption (ML-KEM, ML-DSA). People will use AI to do this.
Why: If the AI makes a security mistake but the program still works, the normal tests will not notice.

What we did (simple words): Build a 'security gate' that checks AI-converted code for the specific mistakes that tests cannot see.
Why: Tests only check that the program works; they do not check that it is safe.

What we did (simple words): Wrote 20 small real-world style programs (file encryption, logins, signatures, tokens...) in old and new encryption, with tests.
Why: To have a fair playground to measure on.

What we did (simple words): Made 77 broken versions with one hidden security mistake each (10 kinds of mistakes).
Why: To check that tests miss them and the gate finds them.

What we did (simple words): Ran the gate and two standard security tools (Semgrep and Bandit) on the 77 broken versions.
Why: To compare our gate with existing tools.
Result: Gate found 71 of 71 original ones (0 false alarms); tests 0, Semgrep 2, Bandit 7. On 6 new ones: gate 4 of 6

What we did (simple words): Asked 4 AI models (3 small local + 1 large online) to convert the 20 programs: 400 conversions.
Why: To see what AI really does.
Result: 84 really converted and passed all tests; gate says 26 of them are insecure (Semgrep 0; Bandit 1)

What we did (simple words): Many AI outputs did not convert at all but still passed all tests.
Why: Shows tests cannot even tell if the conversion happened.
Result: 117 outputs passed tests while still using old encryption

What we did (simple words): An independent AI reviewer (not shown the gate's answers) checked 35 conversions by hand.
Why: To measure how often the gate is correct.
Result: On real conversions the gate caught 5 of 8 real mistakes (63%); 5 of its 6 alarms were right

What we did (simple words): Asked the AI models to fix their insecure code: once with only test results and once with the gate's report.
Why: To see if the gate's report helps fixing.
Result: Test results only: 0 of 31 fixed. Gate report: 10 of 31 fixed (all by the large model, all checked by hand and real)

What we did (simple words): Found small bugs in our own gate (e.g. it did not recognise the name 'ML-KEM' with a hyphen), and the reviewer was an AI not a human.
Why: Research must report its own weaknesses.
Result: Corrected numbers reported next to original ones
